Reporting in from south Louisiana. Very glad to be here, and am comforted by the general sentiment I detect from most users regarding what went wrong at the other place. My question is, are censorship, SJW cancer, safe spaces, corporate control, etc. inevitable results of online communities such as these? Is it possible for this place to exist without being tainted by the such scum?

I'd say it's the inevitable result of a centralized website that needs to be monetized. The one way to completely prevent the problem would be to go back to the old USENET model -- a protocol, rather than a website, owned by everyone. No one party can censor USENET anymore than one party can shut down bit torrent, or the entire world wide web (which, in this case, the technical distinction between the WWW and the internet actually matters).

The major problem with the decentralized model is it would take more work for the users than just firing up a web browser, which is part of why everyone chats on websites now instead of USENET -- the other part being that the old USENET protocol didn't allow for things like moderators with the power to remove spam, let alone shitposting, which is why a new protocol would be needed.
